The 1.3.0 release of the AT-D890UV firmware mods. It applies to the stock **V1.05** package (20260521) only. Everything in 1.2.1 is also in this build.

**What's changed**

- **Quieter Indoor volume range:** the Indoor range now starts at -39 dB at knob level 1 (it was -30 dB), so the bottom of the knob is almost silent. The top of the range is unchanged. The other ranges are unchanged.

**What's fixed**

- **Extra rows in three Radio Set menus:** Settings > Radio Set > Display Func, Key Func and DMR Func each ended with two rows, "Vol Popup" and "Vol Range", that belong only in Voice Func. They are gone: the three menus have their stock rows again (15, 11 and 3), and Voice Func keeps both rows.
- **Graph screens and the S-meter bar flashing:** on a digital channel, with a long contact name scrolling on the last-call line, the channel-screen meter bar, the S-meter screen, Spectrum and Signal graph went black for a moment every two or three seconds. They now stay drawn, and the name still scrolls.

**Checking it worked:** after the radio restarts, Device Info > Mod Ver shows `mm9pdy-1.3.0`. Settings > Radio Set > Display Func ends with its stock last row, with no "Vol Popup" or "Vol Range".

**Going back to stock:** flash stock V1.05 from this page, or use the official CPS.

releases.summary: A 1.2.1 release candidate: S-meter and channel-distance fixes, Busy Lock following the timeslot in use, and two new Bluetooth menu rows (knob volume on/off, internal mic with a headset).
releases.verifyHint: After the radio restarts, Device Info > Mod Ver shows "mm9pdy-1.2.1-rc.1".
releases.notes:
A release candidate for 1.2.1, for testing. It applies to the stock **V1.05** package (20260521) only. Everything in 1.2.0 is also in this build.

**How far it has been checked:** every change in this build has been checked in an emulator only. None of it has been tried on a radio yet, and the emulator has no audio and no Bluetooth link, so the Bluetooth rows in particular need a radio and a headset.

**What's fixed**

- **S-meter on the air band:** on the air band (108–136 MHz) the signal bar is no longer drawn. It used to stay on screen, frozen at its last reading. The full-screen S-meter says it cannot measure there. Leaving the air band brings the bar back with a fresh reading.
- **Channel distance:** the text is no longer cut off at the right edge. The compass point is drawn whole, for example `992km NW` and `9.9mi NW`, where before the last letter was missing or cut.
- **Busy Lock follows the timeslot in use:** after `*`, or on a talk group with its own timeslot, Busy Lock checks the slot the radio is actually using, not the channel's programmed slot. Before, on a digital repeater channel it could refuse to transmit because the other slot was busy, and let you key up over a call on your own slot.

**What's new**

- **BT Knob Vol:** Main Menu > BT has a new row, **BT Knob Vol** (On or Off). On is the default and works as before. Off gives stock behaviour: the volume knob no longer changes the headset volume, and the headset keeps the Bluetooth speaker-gain value from the CPS or the Bluetooth menu. With a headset connected the change applies at once.
- **BT Int Mic:** Main Menu > BT has a new last row, **BT Int Mic** (Off or On). Off is the default and is stock. On means the radio's own PTT transmits from the radio's microphone (or the hand microphone) while a Bluetooth headset is connected. The headset's PTT button and VOX still use the headset's microphone. The first PTT you press decides the microphone for the whole transmission. The emergency alarm's voice still uses the headset microphone, as stock.

**Known limits**

- The Bluetooth rows have not been tried with a real headset. In particular, it is not yet known whether the headset's microphone is fully cut out when BT Int Mic sends the radio's microphone, or whether the sub PTT and the hand microphone's PTT behave like the main PTT.
- Busy Lock and the heard-call record are fixed. Other places where the radio might still use the channel's programmed timeslot instead of the slot in use are being looked at for a later release.

**Checking it worked:** after the radio restarts, Device Info > Mod Ver shows `mm9pdy-1.2.1-rc.1`.

**Going back to stock:** flash stock V1.05 from this page, or use the official CPS.

releases.summary: A 1.2.0 release candidate: rc.3 plus timeslot fixes, S-meter colours, a signal history screen, a spectrum that shows real signals, a zone-scan resume time, and volume ranges with a volume bar.
releases.verifyHint: After the radio restarts, Device Info > Mod Ver shows "mm9pdy-1.2.0-rc.4".
releases.notes:
A release candidate for 1.2.0, for testing. It applies to the stock **V1.05** package (20260521) only. It is 1.2.0-rc.3 with the changes below. Everything in 1.1.0 and 1.2.0-rc.3 is also in this build.

**How far it has been checked:** the S-meter changes have been tried on the owner's radio from test builds, and the spectrum fix was confirmed with a second radio transmitting near the channel. The volume bar and its menu rows have been tried on the owner's radio from a test build; the loudness of the volume ranges hasn't been tuned by ear yet. The other changes, and this exact build, have been checked in an emulator only.

**What's new since 1.2.0-rc.3**

- **T1 / T2 badge:** the red badge next to `CH-n` now shows the timeslot the radio is using. A talk group picked with TG next / previous that has its own timeslot (from its RX group list, or a name ending `TS1` / `TS2`) shows that slot; before, the badge always showed the channel's slot. In the dual display, each side's badge follows that side's talk group.
- **Star key always wins:** a short `*` now switches the timeslot the radio is using, even on a talk group with its own timeslot (from its RX group list or a `TS1` / `TS2` name), and "TS n Selected" and the badge name the slot in use. TG next / previous, or changing channel or zone, goes back to the talk group's own slot, or the channel's when the talk group has none.
- **Slot Switch key:** a key set to the radio's own Slot Switch function now switches from the timeslot in use, as `*` does, and saves it into the channel.
- **The spectrum now shows signals where they are.** In rc.3 the receiver didn't actually move away from the channel during a sweep, so the whole graph rose or fell with whatever was on or near the channel, and no peak appeared. Each point now really retunes the receiver, the same way a scan does, and a signal shows as a peak at its own frequency.
- **S-meter colours:** the bar and the spectrum are coloured by signal level on one fixed scale: dark blue for very weak, then blue, cyan, green, yellow and orange, up to red for strong. A colour always means the same strength, whatever span or range you choose. The bar's peak marker is red.
- **Signal history:** **S-Meter > Signal graph** plots the channel's signal level over time, like a heart monitor: one column every 0.1 second, 16 seconds across the screen. A short blank gap marks "now". **P1** pauses and resumes, **P2** clears, **Back** leaves. The radio stays on your channel while it is open.
- **Spectrum gap:** like the signal history, the spectrum shows a short blank gap just ahead of the point being measured, so you can see where the sweep has got to.
- **Zone scan resume time:** Main Menu > Scan has a new **Zone scan resume** row: 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, 5 s or 10 s. It is how long a zone scan waits on a channel after the activity ends, and after you transmit, before it carries on. The default is 5 s. Before, a zone scan could carry on after a fraction of a second, so a reply was easy to miss.
- **Scan and Scan popup moved:** these two rows are now in Main Menu > Scan, after the stock rows, and keep the value you had. They are no longer in the quick filters menu.
- **Quick filters: Tone match:** the **Tone** row is now called **Tone match** and shows On (the stock behaviour) or Off (any tone opens the squelch).
- **Volume ranges:** a new setting changes how the volume knob maps to loudness. **Indoor** keeps the low end gentle for quiet rooms, **Outdoor** is louder low down, and **Full** spreads the whole range across the knob. **Stock**, the default, is the release's own loudness, so nothing changes until you choose a range. Under a range, the knob fully down is true silence (no hiss, no beeps), and a knob resting near a step no longer flickers between two levels. The knob still sets the volume; the range only changes what each position means. An earpiece and a Bluetooth headset keep their stock levels.
- **Volume bar:** turning the knob shows a bar with the level and, under it, the range in use (`Range: Stock`, `Indoor`, `Outdoor`, `Full`, or `BT` with a headset). Press **Menu** while the bar is up to step to the next range; the loudness changes at once. The bar closes by itself after a few seconds. It doesn't appear over the heard-call card, the quick filters or the menus.
- **New Voice Func rows:** Settings > Radio Set > Voice Func has two new rows at the end. **Vol Popup** turns the volume bar on or off (it is the CPS's volume prompt option, now on the radio). **Vol Range** picks the range: Stock, Indoor, Outdoor or Full.
- **S-Meter menu order:** the screens come first, then the settings: S-Meter screen, Signal graph, Spectrum, Display, Average, Peak hold, Spectrum set.

**Known limits**

- The dBm and S-unit readings, and so the colours, are approximate: the meter isn't calibrated against a signal generator yet. The raw reading and the dB difference on the signal screen are the reliable parts.
- On the air band (108–136 MHz) the radio can't measure signal strength. The spectrum won't start there and the signal history draws nothing, but the signal bar stays on screen with its last reading. That is a bug, still to be fixed.
- The volume ranges' loudness steps are first values, to be tuned on the radio. Expect them to change in a later build.
- The spectrum measures about 25 points a second and stays within the channel's band. During a sweep the main side isn't listening to the channel; **Back** returns it.

**Checking it worked:** after the radio restarts, Device Info > Mod Ver shows `mm9pdy-1.2.0-rc.4`.

**Going back to stock:** flash stock V1.05 from this page, or use the official CPS.

releases.summary: A 1.2.0 release candidate: rc.2 plus an S-meter, with a signal bar on the channel screen, a dedicated signal screen with a difference mode for comparing antennas, and a spectrum screen.
releases.verifyHint: After the radio restarts, Device Info > Mod Ver shows "mm9pdy-1.2.0-rc.3".
releases.notes:
A release candidate for 1.2.0, for testing. It applies to the stock **V1.05** package (20260521) only. It is 1.2.0-rc.2 with the **S-meter** added. Everything in 1.1.0 and 1.2.0-rc.2 is also in this build.

**How far it has been checked:** the S-meter has been tried on the owner's radio from a test build: the bar, the signal screen and the spectrum all respond to a nearby transmitter. This exact build is checked in an emulator only.

**What's new since 1.2.0-rc.2**

- **S-meter menu:** the Main Menu has a new **S-Meter** item at the end. **Display** turns the signal bar on and picks what it shows: Bar, Bar + raw, Bar + dBm or Bar + S (S-units). It is off by default. **Average** smooths the reading (Off, Fast, Slow). **Peak hold** keeps a peak marker for 1 or 3 seconds.
- **Signal bar:** in the single display, a bar under the channel shows the received signal strength, with the reading in the corner. It replaces the last-call lines while it is on. It shows the noise floor as well as signals, so it moves even when nothing is heard.
- **Signal screen:** **S-Meter > S-Meter screen** (or a key assigned to **Satellite Predicting** in the CPS, which this firmware turns into the S-meter key) opens a full-screen meter with a large reading, a scale, and min / max / average. Press **P1** to take the current reading as a reference: the screen then shows the difference in dB, which is handy for comparing antennas. **P2** clears the reference and the min / max. Up and Down change the unit. **Back** leaves it.
- **Spectrum:** **S-Meter > Spectrum** sweeps the main side's receiver across a band around the channel and draws the signal level at each step. **S-Meter > Spectrum set** chooses the span, the step and the top and bottom of the scale. On the screen, **P1** and **P2** change the span and step, Up and Down move a marker that shows its frequency and level, and **Back** stops the sweep and returns the radio to the channel. The backlight stays on while the spectrum is open.

**Known limits**

- The dBm and S-unit readings are approximate: the meter isn't calibrated against a signal generator yet. The raw reading and the dB difference on the signal screen are the reliable parts, so use those to compare antennas.
- On the air band (108–136 MHz) the radio can't measure signal strength. The spectrum won't start there, but the signal bar stays on screen with its last reading. That is a bug, to be fixed.
- The dual display shows no signal bar.
- The spectrum sweeps a few dozen steps a second, and stays within the channel's band.
- During a sweep the main side isn't listening to the channel. Back returns it.

**Checking it worked:** after the radio restarts, Device Info > Mod Ver shows `mm9pdy-1.2.0-rc.3`, and Main Menu ends with **S-Meter**.

**Going back to stock:** flash stock V1.05 from this page, or use the official CPS.

releases.summary: Channel distance, an S-meter with a spectrum and a signal history, a zone-scan resume time, volume ranges with a volume bar, timeslot fixes, and a new single-display layout.
releases.verifyHint: After the radio restarts, Device Info > Mod Ver shows "mm9pdy-1.2.0".
releases.notes:
The 1.2.0 release of the AT-D890UV firmware mods. It applies to the stock **V1.05** package (20260521) only.

It is the same build as release candidate 1.2.0-rc.4, apart from the release name, and rc.4 passed its radio check. Everything in 1.1.0 is also in this build.

**What's new since 1.1.0**

- **Channel distance:** the channel screen shows how far away the current memory channel's site is, and in which direction, from the radio's GPS fix, for example `850m N` or `4.3km NE`. It needs channel positions written by Codeplug Studio's **MM9PDY** target, GPS on and a recent fix.
- **Single display:** one 3-line layout for analogue and digital channels: the channel name, then the talk group or receive frequency, then the zone name on a small line underneath. In the dual display the sub side's line shows its own `Talk group / Zone`.
- **S-meter:** Main Menu > **S-Meter** opens the screens first, then the settings.
  - A signal bar on the channel screen, coloured by level, with a raw, dBm or S-unit reading.
  - A full-screen meter with min / max / average and a difference mode for comparing antennas.
  - A **spectrum** that sweeps the receiver around the channel and shows signals as peaks at their own frequency.
  - A **signal history** that plots the channel's level over time, like a heart monitor.
  - One fixed colour scale everywhere, so a colour always means the same strength.
- **Zone scan resume time:** Main Menu > Scan > **Zone scan resume** (0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, 5 s or 10 s; default 5 s) sets how long a zone scan waits on a channel after the activity ends, and after you transmit, before it carries on. Before, it could carry on after a fraction of a second.
- **Heard-call popup:** a zone scan that holds on a DMR call shows who and which talk group. **Scan** (Zone / List) and **Scan popup** are rows of Main Menu > Scan.
- **Timeslots:** the T1 / T2 badge shows the slot in use, a short `*` always switches it, and a Slot Switch key does the same and saves it into the channel.
- **Volume:** **Vol Range** (Stock, Indoor, Outdoor, Full) changes how the knob maps to loudness, with true silence at the bottom of a range. An optional volume bar shows the level and range when you turn the knob; press **Menu** on it to step the range. Both settings are rows of Settings > Radio Set > Voice Func. With a Bluetooth headset connected, the knob sets the headset's volume.
- **Quick filters:** **Tone match: On / Off** (Off opens the squelch of a toned analogue channel on any signal) and **To VFO: Copy** (copies the main side's channel into its VFO).

**Known limits**

- The channel distance text can clip at the right, and the dual display shows no distance.
- The S-meter's dBm, S-units and colours are approximate until it is calibrated. On the air band the signal bar stays on screen with its last reading. During a spectrum sweep the main side isn't listening to the channel.
- The volume ranges' loudness steps are first values and may change in a later release.
- A channel with no contact must store "none" within 0–9999 (Codeplug Studio writes 9999).

**Checking it worked:** after the radio restarts, Device Info > Mod Ver shows `mm9pdy-1.2.0`.

**Going back to stock:** flash stock V1.05 from this page, or use the official CPS.

releases.notes:
The 1.1.0 release of the AT-D890UV firmware mods. It applies to the stock **V1.05** package (20260521) only.

- **Mod version:** the power-on screen shows `mm9pdy-1.1.0`, and Menu > Settings > Device Info has a **Mod Ver:** item with the same text. Firmware Ver: still shows the stock `Ver 1.05`.
- **TG Next / TG Previous during a call:** step off a busy talk group while a call is being received. Main side and digital memory channels only; they do nothing while the sub side is receiving.

releases.verifyHint: Settings > Device Info > Versions shows "mm9pdy-1.2.0-rc.1" under DM32.01.L01.048.
releases.notes:
A release candidate for 1.2.0, for testing. It applies to stock firmware **v1.01.048** only. Everything in 1.1.0 is also in this build.

**Not yet tried on a radio:** the new items below are checked in an emulator only.

**What's new since 1.1.0**

- **Channel distance:** the zone-name row shows how far away the current memory channel's site is, and in which direction, from the radio's GPS position, for example `4.3km NE`. It needs channel positions written by Codeplug Studio's **MM9PDY** target, GNSS on and a recent fix. Power-cycle the radio after the write: it reads the positions at power-on. VFO, zone scan and channels with no position show nothing.
- **A timeslot per RX group list member:** Codeplug Studio's MM9PDY target can store a slot for each member of an RX group list. Step to that talk group with TG Prev / TG Next and the radio uses that slot. It wins over a `TS1` / `TS2` name suffix; the star key still overrides both.
- **Quick menu rows RX match and TS filter,** under Light mode. **RX match** (TG / RGL / Any) sets which group calls you hear; RGL is stock. **TS filter** (On / Off): Off also listens on the other timeslot when both are quiet; On is stock.

- A 16-character zone name leaves no room for the distance, so none is shown.
- If you change an RX group list's members in another tool, such as the official CPS, the radio ignores that list's stored slots until Studio writes them again.
- TS filter Off is a test feature: PTT always goes out on the channel's own slot.
- RX match TG applies from the next call after a talk-group step. The Monitor key still opens the radio to every call.

**Checking it worked:** Settings > Device Info > Versions shows `mm9pdy-1.2.0-rc.1` under Baofeng's `DM32.01.L01.048`.

**Going back to stock:** flash stock v1.01.048 from this page, or use the official CPS.

releases.summary: Talk-group keys that step through the RX group list, the PTT contact on screen, a star-key timeslot swap with a TS1/TS2 badge, a timeslot from a talk-group name suffix, and the mod version in Device Info.
releases.verifyHint: Settings > Device Info > Versions shows "mm9pdy-1.1.0" under DM32.01.L01.048.
releases.notes:
The 1.1.0 release of the DM-32UV firmware mods. It applies to stock firmware **v1.01.048** only. It is about DMR: change who you're talking to and which timeslot you're on from the front panel. Everything in 1.0.0 is also in this build.

The codeplug format is unchanged, so the official CPS and Codeplug Studio read and write the radio as before, and the radio keeps its channels and settings across the update.

**How far it has been checked:** every feature passes the emulator test suite, and the release was checked on the owner's radio before it shipped. The full on-air checklist (which slot actually goes out, for example) is still open.

**What's new since 1.0.0**

- **Talk groups without reprogramming:** assign two keys to **Previous Record** and **Next Record** in the CPS (the radio lists them as **TG Prev** and **TG Next**). On a digital channel with an RX group list they step through its members, and PTT calls the one you picked. Nothing is saved: power off and every channel is back to its own contact.
- **See who you're calling:** on a digital channel, the line under the channel name shows the contact PTT will call instead of the frequency.
- **Star-key timeslot swap:** a short press of `*` on a digital repeater channel swaps between TS1 and TS2 until you change channel, step talk group or power off. On analogue channels `*` still toggles NOAA weather.
- **Timeslot badge:** `TS1` or `TS2` next to the `DIG` badge, showing the slot the radio is actually using.
- **Timeslot from a talk-group name:** a contact named, for example, `Scotland TS2` switches to that slot when you step to it. The name is shown without the suffix.
- **Mod version:** `mm9pdy-1.1.0` at the bottom of the boot screen and under Settings > Device Info > Versions.

**Known limits**

- While scanning, the second line shows the frequency, not a talk-group name.
- After a channel change, the frequency can flash for a moment before the contact name appears.
- A contact name that happens to end in `ts1` or `ts2` sets the slot; there is no switch to turn that off.
- In dual watch with both sides on the same channel, a star-key swap can sometimes outlive a channel change on one side.

**Checking it worked:** Settings > Device Info > Versions shows `mm9pdy-1.1.0` under Baofeng's `DM32.01.L01.048`.

**Going back to stock:** flash stock v1.01.048 from this page, or use the official CPS.

releases.summary: Zone scan on channels without a scan list, a quick menu with light mode, position-report retry, a GPS padding fix and menu text fixes.
releases.verifyHint: Press Scan on a channel with no scan list: a zone scan should start. Device information still reads DM32.01.L01.048; that is expected.
releases.notes:
The first full release of the DM-32UV firmware mods. It applies to stock firmware **v1.01.048** only.

Everything not listed here behaves exactly as stock. The codeplug format is unchanged, so the official CPS and Codeplug
Studio read and write the radio as before, and the radio keeps its channels and settings across the update.

**What's in it**

- **Zone scan:** pressing Scan on a channel with no scan list scans the whole current zone (up to 64 channels) instead
  of refusing. While it walks, the screen shows the zone name and `Scanning...`. It resumes about 5 s after a signal
  ends. Channels with a scan list scan it exactly as stock. Tested on the radio.
- **Quick menu and light mode:** assign the stock **Flashlight** key function to a free programmable key (SK1, SK2 or
  P1; avoid P2). It opens a small menu with one row, **Light mode**, which inverts the screen for easier reading in
  daylight. The choice is saved across power-off. Tested on the radio.
- **Position report retry:** a timed position report now waits for a GPS fix instead of being skipped until the next
  interval, so a 300 s interval actually sends. Tested on the radio.
- **GPS position padding fix:** Fixed Beacon position reports keep leading zeros in latitude and longitude, so APRS
  gateways can read them. A community fix (IU2VTP). Emulator and byte checks only.
- **Text fixes:** eleven English typos and wording fixes in menus and pop-ups, for example "VerSions" → "Versions" and
  "Nonsupport" → "Unsupported". Checked byte for byte; not every screen has been looked at on the radio.

**Known limits:** nuisance delete during a zone scan is untested, and the zone-scan hang time is fixed at about 5 s.

**Checking it worked:** the radio does not show the mod's version yet. Device information still reads
`DM32.01.L01.048`. Check that Scan on a channel with no scan list starts a zone scan.

**Going back to stock:** flash stock v1.01.048 from this page, or use the official CPS.

releases.summary: Fixes the radio's menus freezing the screen and keys.
releases.verifyHint: The bottom of the power-on screen shows "MM9PDY-1.1.1".
releases.notes:
Release 1.1.1 of the Retevis RT95 front-panel modification. It applies to the stock front-panel firmware **LCD V1.41** (20231202) only, and leaves the radio board's firmware alone. Everything in 1.1.0 is unchanged apart from the fix below.

**How far it has been checked:** this build has been checked in an emulator, including a new test that opens the FUNC menu and goes into and out of every item. A test build of the same fix was written to a radio with Codeplug Studio and the menus were used on it before this release was made. There was no separate release candidate.

**Fixed**

- **Menus froze the radio.** On 1.1.0, opening the radio's own menus (the FUNC menu, the channel menu and others) and picking an item could freeze the screen and every key, power included, until the battery or DC power was removed. Audio kept working. The menus now work as on the stock firmware.

**Known issues** (still open, to be fixed in a later release)

- In the zone selector, some zone names run past the end of the box and leave a few pixels on the screen near the P6 label. Some names flicker and are not drawn.
- Switching zone stays on the current channel if it also belongs to the new zone, instead of going to the channel you last used in that zone.
- The channel number shown is the radio's own number, not the channel's place in the zone.

**Known limits**

- Screen flip stays in the radio's FUNC menu (DIR). A key set to DIR opens zones instead.
- A description is hidden once the channel has been changed on the radio or with another programming tool. Write again from Studio to bring it back.
- Without zone data from Studio, the radio behaves as before, with all channels.

**Checking it worked:** switch the radio off and on and read the bottom of the power-on screen: it shows `MM9PDY-1.1.1`.

**Going back:** write release 1.1.0, or the maker's stock front-panel firmware (LCD V1.41), with Codeplug Studio. Avoid 1.1.0 if you use the radio's menus.

releases.summary: Zones, channel descriptions and a tidier single-watch screen.

**What's new**

- **Zones:** group your channels into up to 32 named zones in Codeplug Studio, with the *Retevis RT95 VOX (MM9PDY modded firmware)* target. A programmable key set to DIR shows `ZON` and opens the zone selector. The knob, the microphone's Up and Down keys and scan stay inside the zone. Each side keeps its own zone, and the radio remembers it when switched off. Studio can set the key for you ("Put Zone on a P-key").
- **Channel descriptions:** a short description per channel (up to 12 characters, from the channel's Name in Studio) shows under the channel name in single watch.
- **Single-watch screen:** the main side is drawn where it sits in dual watch, so the zone name (sky blue) and the description (amber) fit underneath. Dual watch is unchanged.

**Known issues** (to be fixed in 1.1.1)

- In the zone selector, some zone names run past the end of the box and leave a few pixels on the screen near the P6 label. Some names flicker and are not drawn.
- Switching zone stays on the current channel if it also belongs to the new zone, instead of going to the channel you last used in that zone.
- The channel number shown is the radio's own number, not the channel's place in the zone.

**Known limits**

- Screen flip stays in the radio's FUNC menu (DIR). A key set to DIR opens zones instead.
- A description is hidden once the channel has been changed on the radio or with another programming tool. Write again from Studio to bring it back.
- Without zone data from Studio, the radio behaves as before, with all channels.

**Checking it worked:** switch the radio off and on and read the bottom of the power-on screen: it shows `MM9PDY-1.1.0`.

**Going back:** write release 1.0.0-rc.2, or the maker's stock front-panel firmware (LCD V1.41), with Codeplug Studio.

releases.summary: Release candidate 2: the first published build. The radio works as stock, and the power-on screen shows which firmware is installed.
releases.verifyHint: The bottom of the power-on screen shows "MM9PDY-1.0.0-RC.2".
releases.notes:
The first release candidate of the Retevis RT95 front-panel modification, for testing. It applies to the stock front-panel firmware **LCD V1.41** (20231202) only, and leaves the radio board's firmware alone.

**How far it has been checked:** this exact build has been checked in an emulator only. A test build that differs from it only in the version line was written to a radio once with Codeplug Studio and worked. Nothing else has been tried on a radio.

**What's in it**

- **Everything else as stock:** the radio works as it does with the maker's front-panel firmware. The channels, the menus and the radio's own version text are unchanged.
- **Version on the power-on screen:** the bottom of the power-on screen shows `MM9PDY-1.0.0-RC.2`, so you can tell which firmware is installed. The radio's small text is capitals only.

**Known limits**

- The version line is only on the power-on screen, for as long as that screen stays up.
- The test screen (**FUNC** and **P4**) keeps showing the maker's version text. That is expected.

**Checking it worked:** switch the radio off and on and read the bottom of the power-on screen: it shows `MM9PDY-1.0.0-RC.2`.

**Going back to stock:** write the maker's stock front-panel firmware (LCD V1.41) again with Codeplug Studio, or use the maker's own tool.
